articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Razaullah hitting makes home side wait for third-Test win at Edgbaston
articles.summary: England face a chase of 130 to win the third Test after Pakistan debutant Razaullah produces some thrilling resistance on day three at Edgbaston.
articles.body:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day three of five)

Pakistan 133 (Tongue 4-42) & 449 (Masood 95, Razaullah 81, Babar 76, Awais 59)

England 453 (Brook 75, Smith 69, Lawrence 65, Gay 60, Robinson 50; Razaullah 4-148)

England face a chase of 130 to win the third Test after Pakistan debutant Razaullah produced some thrilling resistance on day three at Edgbaston.

Pakistan had battled to 318-8, still two runs behind, with potentially more than two hours of play remaining when Razaullah, the tourists' number nine, launched a sensational assault.

The 21-year-old's audacious 81 from 63 balls frazzled England and propelled Pakistan to 449. His nine sixes tied Ben Stokes' record for the number of maximums in a Test innings in England.

Razaullah shared an ninth-wicket stand of 121 with Muhammad Abbas, who whacked two sixes of his own in his 42. Finally, Razaullah was stumped off Lawrence to end the day and signal the beginning of England's chase on Saturday.

Pakistan deserved to drag the match into a weekend, restoring a modicum of pride to what has been a shambolic tour.

England might have won inside two days had it not been for bad weather on Thursday. From 55-2 overnight, 268 behind, Pakistan did not capitulate on Friday.

Shan Masood and Azan Awais extended their third-wicket stand to 125 until Awais tickled the off-spin of Dan Lawrence down the leg side for 59.

Masood added another 89 with captain Babar Azam. The left-hander was denied a century on 95 when Lawrence took a spectacular one-handed catch at gully off Gus Atkinson.

Babar was classy for his 76, yet was discomforted when England went to a short-ball plan either side of tea. His dismissal to a Josh Tongue bouncer seemed to confirm a three-day finish, but Razaullah had other ideas.

Razaullah introduces himself as Pakistan thrive in the madness

'Out of control' - Cook questions England tactics

On what could have been the final day of a disappointing series, a Test match broke out. The contest between bat and ball was even and compelling, and the Hollies Stand filled Edgbaston with an atmosphere missing from the first two days.

In their last act of a miserable tour, Pakistan showed what they are made of. Until Razaullah flayed them, England did not bowl badly - the hosts were simply met with patience, bravery and sound judgement from the touring top order.

Despite being bowled out for 133 on day one and reduced to 0-2 in their second innings, Pakistan are alive. England should win, though the tourists will have a target to defend. The run chase could be ticklish.

Razaullah was one of the seven players Pakistan drafted into the squad for this Test. He first impressed with his pace bowling in England's first innings, then provided grandstand entertainment late on Friday evening.

After a first full day in the field this series, England faded. As Razaullah and Abbas swung and swiped, England's bowlers simply could not hit the stumps. Joe Root's decision to employ Lawrence with the second new-ball was curious.

England were left frustrated and devoid of ideas. For everyone else, it was tremendous fun. Saturday might yet be something special.

Pakistan could have been humiliated in Birmingham, so the performance they produced on Friday was a staggering turnaround. This was the first time they have made more than 200 or batted more than 51 overs in the series.

At 21, Awais looks a prospect and played nicely through the off side. Masood was composed and unfortunate to miss out on a century in what is likely his final Test in the country where he went to school.

Babar showed glimpses of his class, only to lose concentration when England went to bouncers - the captain's dismissal was the first of four wickets to fall for 40 runs.

What came next was remarkable. Razaullah struck the ball clean and long. It started as freewheeling hitting and turned into a match-changing innings. He equalled the record held by New Zealand's Tim Southee for the most sixes in an innings by a Test debutant.

Atkinson was belted into the Edgbaston building site as part of three maximums in the same over, while Jofra Archer was hit back over his head for successive sixes.

Even Abbas got in on the fun. He played reverse-sweeps off Lawrence and clobbered Ollie Robinson over cow corner for two sixes.

As the light faded, it seemed as though the ninth-wicket pair might reach the close, only for Abbas to poke Tongue to point.

In a frantic finish, Razaullah cracked Lawrence for the record-equalling ninth six, drew huge cheers when he overturned being given lbw, then was stumped. He left to a rapturous ovation, a new star of Pakistan cricket.

England's attack have had it all their own way this series. Root's tactics, often criticised in his first spell as captain, have rarely been tested. Friday's chaos will bring plenty of questions for this new regime.

The hosts' efforts for the majority of the day were adequate - they were simply repelled by some quality Pakistan batting. When the ball moved, England held their length, then went to a short-ball plan at the right time and took some sharp catches.

But when Razaullah and Abbas came together, England lost the plot. The field was scattered for bouncers and, when the bowlers tried to target the stumps, they either missed the target or were met by stout Pakistan defence.

Robinson has been in the form of his life, yet was somehow ignored for the second new-ball in favour of Lawrence. Archer could not hide his frustration at the treatment he received from Razaullah, while Root briefly left the field.

By the end, England were reduced to Atkinson bowling bouncers at Razaullah with eight fielders on the boundary.

The late wickets were a huge relief. England dragged themselves off the field, chastened, though still in line for a 3-0 clean sweep.

articles.title: Pakistan stun England with stunning fightback as Razaullah and Abbas force tricky chase at Edgbaston
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan produced a remarkable fightback on Day 3 of the third Test at Edgbaston, turning what looked like a straightforward innings defeat into a pot.
articles.body: Pakistan produced a remarkable fightback on Day 3 of the third Test at Edgbaston, turning what looked like a straightforward innings defeat into a potentially tricky chase for England.After being bowled out for just 133 in their first innings and conceding a 320-run lead, Pakistan were expected to fold quickly in their second innings. Instead, they battled for nearly 97 overs and were eventually dismissed for 449, leaving England a target of 130 runs to win the Test and complete a 3-0 series clean sweep.The result means England will return on Day 4 needing only 130 runs, but Pakistan's extraordinary lower-order resistance ensured the hosts could not finish the match on the third evening.Masood, Babar and Azan lead Pakistan's fightbackPakistan's recovery was built around contributions from their top and middle order.Captain Shan Masood narrowly missed out on a century, scoring a determined 95 to anchor the innings. Azan Awais added 59, while Babar Azam played an assured knock of 76 as Pakistan steadily erased England's huge first-innings advantage.Just when Pakistan appeared to have done enough to force England to bat again, wickets began to tumble and England sensed another opportunity to wrap up the Test. But the lower order had other ideas.Razaullah and Abbas produce stunning 121-run standDebutant Razaullah delivered the biggest surprise of the day with a sensational counter-attacking 81 from 73 balls.Batting at No. 9, Razaullah took the attack to England's bowlers and struck nine sixes during his entertaining innings. He found an unlikely but hugely valuable partner in Mohammad Abbas, who held his end together as the pair added 121 runs for the ninth wicket.The partnership stunned England and frustrated their attempts to complete a series sweep on the third day.England eventually broke the stand when Josh Tongue dismissed Abbas, ending one of the most unexpected partnerships of the Test. Razaullah's innings also came to an end shortly afterwards as England's bowlers finally cleaned up the tail.Gus Atkinson played a key role in the late breakthroughs, while Jofra Archer and Tongue had earlier kept Pakistan's batters under pressure.Pakistan's 449 meant England were left with 130 to win. While the target remains modest, the visitors' extraordinary fightback has at least forced England to bat again after their first-innings dominance.England now have a clear opportunity to complete a 3-0 series victory on Day 4. Pakistan, meanwhile, will hope their lower-order heroics have given them enough momentum to create one final twist in a Test that appeared to be heading towards an early finish.Brief scores: Pakistan 133 & 449; England 453. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Razaullah, 21, hits remarkable 81 off 63 balls featuring nine sixes to force final Test into fourth day
articles.summary: Dan Lawrence dismisses Razaullah (81 off 63 balls) with what proves to be the last ball of day three; Pakistan all out for 449 after battling second innings; England set 130 to win on day four - watch live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Saturday
articles.body:
Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

He shared in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42), who himself hit two sixes before picking out point off Josh Tongue in the closing overs, while Razaullah's fun was finally ended - and the day's play - as he was stumped off Dan Lawrence (2-17).

England, guilty of losing the plot in the final session, will now look to chase down 130 on day four, a far stiffer target than initially looked likely, albeit one they should still reel in to clinch a first ever home series whitewash of Pakistan.

The tourists might be cursing not testing England further, with Shan Masood (95) and Babar Azam (76) both spurning golden opportunities to score the first century of the series.

While Masood can count himself a touch unfortunate, out to a screamer of a catch by Lawrence - one-handed, diving low to his right in the slips - Babar's dismissal was much more of a head-scratcher, the captain walking straight into an obvious short-ball trap set by England on the stroke of tea.

That wicket had seemed to signal the end of the Pakistan resistance, with four wickets falling for 40 runs before Razaullah very much had other plans and pushed things into a fourth day with some almighty swings of the bat.

Resuming the third morning on 52-2, the visitors had been watchful to start, with only 15 runs added from a rather sedate opening 7.2 overs, before they suddenly sparked into life and smashed 117 off the next 20 - the wicket of Azan Awais (59) to a feathered edge down leg off Lawrence the only blot on their morning's work.

England's four-pronged pace attack hadn't experienced such a session of toil this series without reward, but were improved after the lunch interval, with Gus Atkinson's initial eight-over burst particularly impressive as he finally secured his second wicket of the series, Masood undone by Lawrence's brilliance in the slips.

Babar was Pakistan's next bright hope for a hundred, what would have been his first in Test cricket for almost four years, but England turned to Jofra Archer and Tongue for a bit of bouncer theory and Babar simply couldn't resist taking it on despite repeated warnings.

It was Tongue (2-106) who finally got his man, Babar gloving one behind, while Archer (1-120) accounted for Saud Shakeel (29) soon after the tea break with another brute of a short ball that he could only balloon to short-leg.

A couple of terrific catches from Jordan Cox behind the stumps then accounted for debutants Ghazi Ghori (16) and Mohammad Imran (4) as Atkinson (3-109) located their inside and outside edges, respectively.

But Pakistan's third debutant, Razaullah, having already impressed with the ball - claiming four first-innings wickets, including that of England's leading Test run-scorer Joe Root in his first over - put on yet another show with an extraordinary display of ball-striking to not only see his side into a lead, but a 129-run advantage at that.

Beyond even his boundary-clearing blitz, there was terrific drama late on when he had an lbw decision against Lawrence overturned on review, only for him to perish the very next ball and what would prove to be the last of the day.

Razaullah: I just had to bat and get Pakistan another day

Razaullah , speaking to Sky Sports Cricket after his 81 off 63 balls:

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who got to enjoy it.

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though.

"I was just trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I won't give any messages to the batters - they can do their bit - but I really, really enjoyed it.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Urooj: Razaullah provided spark | 'Pakistan have to believe'

"That was simply sensational. A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket.

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the [squad] list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green - Joe Root is his first Test wicket, a four-for on debut, and then 81 with nine sixes - all of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet.

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know. Razaullah provides Pakistan a point of difference with pace, and they'll have to believe."

articles.title: Razaullah: 'Razball' reigns as Pakistan thrive in chaos against England on day three at Edgbaston
articles.summary: Cancel the tee time at the Belfry, rearrange the trip to Cadbury World and abort the shopping jolly to the Bullring - Pakistan's debutant Razaullah lights up Edgbaston to send third Test into fourth day.
articles.body:
Cancel the tee time at the Belfry, rearrange the trip to Cadbury World and abort the shopping jolly to the Bullring.

The reason? Pakistan's new star Razaullah and 'Razball'.

England's bowlers were thwarted by a Pakistan side who mixed batting belligerence with brilliance and instead of a Saturday off must reconvene at Edgbaston for day four.

The brilliance was provided by Razaullah, who produced a dizzying knock to breathe life into the third Test and lift the spirits of Pakistan supporters everywhere. A new hero, a new hope.

Bazball might be on its way out, but Birmingham might just have witnessed the birth of a new phenomenon during two hours of unbridled chaos where the Test debutant made a stunning 81 off 63 balls coming in at number nine.

A raw 21-year-old with just eight first-class matches to his name, selected more as a tearaway fast bowler reminiscent of Waqar Younis, Razaullah was probably not a name on the radar of England's bowlers when he was called up amid wholesale changes made by Pakistan before the final Test.

After some blistering strokeplay when he took down the home side's attack, they certainly know who he is now.

There were shades of Shahid Afridi or Abdul Razzaq in the flamboyant nature of the way Razaullah flayed England to all parts.

He took three bats to the crease but broke two with his explosive hitting.

"It's the first time he's been out there for Pakistan ever, and he absolutely lights up the show. This is the attitude that was needed," said former Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja on BBC Test Match Special.

"Someone with a strong body language and who believes in himself. They'll want him playing all formats because he's a natural in mind, body language and attitude. It was a tremendous fightback."

'Out of control' - Cook questions England tactics

England need 130 after thrilling Razaullah hitting

At times when Razaullah - who has one first-class century - was teeing off, England captain Joe Root wore the expression of a chess player waiting for someone to tell him it was his move.

Root stationed eight fielders on the boundary at one point - but it did not deter Razaullah as he brashly swaggered at the crease with the arrogance of youth.

Razaullah's nine sixes is the joint-most ever in a Test innings in England. The other is Ben Stokes' famous 155 with nine against Australia in the Ashes Test in 2023.

He hit as many sixes as Sir Geoffrey Boycott did in his 108-Test career.

Perhaps being so far behind, and expected to capitulate, liberated Pakistan. There was a freedom to their batting hitherto unseen in this series so far.

Shan Masood played with admirable application with a stoic 95 while captain Babar Azam, a weight lifted off his shoulders, made 76.

Yet it was the swashbuckling Razaullah who really captured the imagination.

"England are going to win this Test match, I'm sure," said former England captain Michael Vaughan.

"But Razaullah has given Pakistan cricket some hope. They've unearthed a gem and he will be a superstar for many years."

Even Razaullah's dismissal was pure theatre lapped up by the crowd. Reprieved lbw to Dan Lawrence he danced down the pitch and was stumped next ball.

The young Pakastani left the field to the warmest ovation.

In another world he might have been playing for Cleethorpes in the Yorkshire Cricket Southern Premier League, having signed for the 2026 season only to be called up to a national training camp in May.

Those with tickets for Saturday must have thought the prospect of seeing any play was remote when Pakistan offered a meek surrender on day one.

Steamrolled for 133 just after lunch in Birmingham on Wednesday they looked rudderless against opponents who were ruthless.

Doubtless many punters will have started to make other plans in the expectation this would all be over swiftly, especially when England racked up 453.

Yet with 129 to defend, Pakistan have an outside chance of what would be the most famous of victories.

It's tempting to look at Pakistan cricket through a certain prism, but when moments like these arrive it's impossible not to. Through the emotional wringer again - despair to hope in the space of three days.

"There wouldn't be any person in the world that would've thought we'd go to day four," added Vaughan.

"That is what Pakistan cricket is. They have had a difficult few weeks. The team has been in turmoil. That is why I love Pakistan cricket.

"England will look back at a lot of the tactics and realise they got it wrong. The short stuff, one over of spin, the second new ball with the spinner.

"That day today will make the England team realise there is a long way to go to be world class."

articles.title: Women's Asia Cup: Sri Lanka fight back from 33/4 to beat Pakistan by 4 wickets, set up India final
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Defending champions Sri Lanka produced a remarkable fightback under pressure to beat Pakistan by four wickets and book their place in the W.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defending champions Sri Lanka produced a remarkable fightback under pressure to beat Pakistan by four wickets and book their place in the Women’s Asia Cup final, where they will face India in a repeat of the 2024 summit clash.Chasing 131 at the Dubai International Stadium on Friday, Sri Lanka slumped to 33/4 inside seven overs before Harshitha Samarawickrama and Kavisha Dilhari launched a stirring recovery. The pair added 67 runs for the fifth wicket to bring Sri Lanka within touching distance of victory.Pakistan captain Fatima Sana briefly reignited her side’s hopes by dismissing both batters in the 17th over, leaving Sri Lanka at 109/6 and still needing 22 runs from the final three overs. But Nilakshika Silva and Kaushani Nuthyangana held their nerve to finish the chase with eight balls to spare.Sri Lanka reached 131/6 in 18.4 overs, with Nilakshika unbeaten on 18 off 10 balls and Nuthyangana 10 not out from four deliveries.Harshitha, Dilhari rescue Sri LankaPakistan had made a competitive 130/5 after being asked to bat first. They too had endured a difficult start, slipping to 52/4 inside 10 overs before Fatima Sana’s unbeaten 47 off 36 balls helped revive the innings.Shawaal Zulfiqar provided early momentum with a 24 off 16 balls, while Gull Feroza made 21. But Sri Lanka’s bowlers kept Pakistan under pressure, with Chamari Athapaththu and Chamudi Praboda taking two wickets apiece and Sugandika Kumari claiming one.Sri Lanka’s chase then appeared to be heading towards trouble when Fatima removed Athapaththu and Sanjana Kavindi with successive deliveries in the second over. Hasini Perera and Imesha Dulani also fell quickly, leaving the defending champions four down.Harshitha and Dilhari changed the complexion of the chase with their 67-run stand. Harshitha made 36 from 31 balls, while Dilhari scored 33 off 33, repeatedly finding singles and rotating the strike to absorb the pressure.“The way Harshitha and Kavisha batted, it's amazing. They absorbed the pressure, they took singles and played really good. Under pressure, that partnership was match winning,” Sri Lanka captain Athapaththu said after the game.Fatima, who was named Player of the Match for her 4/38 and unbeaten 47, struck again to remove both set batters. But Pakistan could not close out the game.“Most of the things went well, but the last bit, (the) Sri Lankan middle order took the game away,” Fatima said. “I think the way Harshitha and Kavisha played... They are good in (taking) singles. So credit goes to them.”Repeat of 2024 final awaitsThe victory takes Sri Lanka into their third consecutive Women’s Asia Cup final. They will once again face India, who defeated Bangladesh by 40 runs in their semi-final and have remained unbeaten in the tournament.Sri Lanka defeated India by eight wickets in the 2024 final to claim their maiden Asia Cup title. India, meanwhile, will be chasing a record-extending eighth crown when the two sides meet on Sunday.Athapaththu believes Sri Lanka have enough depth to challenge India again.“We have good finishers like Harshitha, Nilakshika, Kavisha. Most of the players are playing really good, even the bowling unit. So we have good players. So if we can execute our plans in the final, I think we can beat any team,” she said.For Pakistan, the defeat ended their campaign after an inconsistent tournament, while Sri Lanka’s ability to recover from 33/4 once again underlined the resilience that has taken them back to the Asia Cup final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Alastair Cook and Michael Vaughan question Joe Root tactics in Razaullah onslaught
articles.summary: England had “no plan” and were “out of control” in the face of Razaullah’s stunning hitting on the third day of the final Test against Pakistan, according to former captain Alastair Cook.
articles.body:
England had "no plan" and were "out of control" in the face of Razaullah's stunning hitting on the third day of the final Test against Pakistan, according to former captain Alastair Cook.

Razaullah, the 21-year-old batting at number nine on Test debut, clobbered 81 from 63 balls at Edgbaston.

He shared a ninth-wicket partnership of 121 with Muhammad Abbas to drag the third Test into an unlikely fourth day, with England set 130 for victory.

Though the hosts are heavy favourites to earn a 3-0 clean sweep, the carnage of the final session was an alarming spell as Joe Root begins his second spell as captain.

Root's tactics were often criticised in his first spell as skipper and there were further questions of the Yorkshireman when he stood in for former captain Ben Stokes earlier this summer.

"You can get done by the tail - it's very hard when people have the license and ability to hit sixes," Cook told Test Match Special. "What I saw was no plan, it got out of control.

"That's when you need the backroom staff and coaches to step up. I would loved to have seen a message and some real leadership from the coaches."

Razaullah introduces himself as Pakistan thrive in chaos

England need 130 after thrilling Razaullah hitting

England are currently led by interim head coach Marcus Trescothick, with New Zealander Stephen Fleming due to take on the role from December's tour of South Africa.

Trescothick is assisted by bowling coach Tim Southee, who was seen on the boundary rope at times during the partnership.

England's tactics were curious throughout the Razaullah-Abbas partnership. The seamers often stuck to a short-ball plan, with fielders back on the boundary. When their pace bowlers tried to hit the stumps, they could not find the target.

More bizarre was Root giving the second new-ball to part-time off-spinner Dan Lawrence, who had barely bowled in the series to that point. In doing so, Root bowled Lawrence in front of seamer Ollie Robinson, who has had a sensational summer as England's attack leader.

Jonathan Agnew, the former England fast bowler and the BBC's chief cricket commentator, called the tactics "appalling".

"You cannot and should not bowl like that to tailenders as soon as they come in," he said.

"You have to set the tone when you're bowling against tailenders. Yes, you bowl aggressively, but in a controlled way. They are numbers nine and 10 for a reason. It was bitterly disappointing.

"Dan Lawrence is a part-time off-spinner and he took the second new-ball. If you're looking for any aspect of the day that is utterly bonkers, that is it."

Razaullah's thrilling knock included nine sixes, tying the record for the most maximums in an innings by a batter on Test debut.

He also equalled Stokes' record for the most sixes in a Test played in England.

There were times when Root looked devoid of ideas, while the energy was sapped from his team. Jofra Archer cut a frustrated figure when Razaullah hit him for successive straight sixes and at one point Gus Atkinson was asked to bowl bouncers with eight fielders on the boundary.

"We shouldn't be surprised by England, they've delivered tactically like this on a regular basis," said ex-England captain Michael Vaughan.

"I think they'll win this game but they can't keep making mistakes like that. The basics of Test cricket generally work and that's to hit the top of the stumps. It's a bit of a warning sign that this attack is very good but they aren't the finished article just yet.

"Who are the characters in the team who are going got grab a hold of everyone and say, 'right, I'm going to make a moment'. I didn't see it from anyone today."

At one stage Root left the field for an opportunity to consult with the England backroom staff, although it did little to alter the course of the evening.

Eventually, Abbas poked the pace of Josh Tongue to point before Razaullah was stumped off Lawrence from the final ball of the day to leave Pakistan 453 all out.

"I'm disappointed, of course," said Trescothick. "We were in a position where they were eight down and the scores were level. We were hoping to go through them pretty quickly.

"We tried many different things. You have variations of plans. We bowled the short ball for a period of time, then length for a period of time, then a bit of spin. You're always chopping and changing, with various ideas.

"You'd always like to think you can do it better and you analyse it afterwards saying, 'right, was there an area or tactic we missed to get it right?' You hope in those situations when you bowl it in the right place, which we did on many occasions, that you get the nick or bowl them. Fair play, they played pretty well."

articles.summary: Urooj Mumtaz lauded "a perfectly written first chapter" in Razaullah's Test career as he notched a stunning 81 off 63 balls on debut, smashing nine sixes; England set 130 to win on day four - watch live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Saturday
articles.body:
Razaullah, who has only played eight previous first-class matches in his career, smacked nine sixes in his remarkable innings, equalling Tim Southee's record for the most maximums for a Test debutant, dazzling in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42) that eventually propelled Pakistan to a total of 449 and set England a target of 130.

The 21-year-old consolidated an already impressive performance on debut with the ball, taking four wickets in England's innings, including that of skipper Joe Root for his first.

His performance with the bat was undoubtedly the deciding factor in forcing the match into a fourth day that looked so improbable when he arrived at the crease, when Pakistan trailed by two runs at 318-8.

"His innings was simply sensational," Mumtaz said on Sky Sports. "A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket!

"One 21-year-old who wasn't even on the list gets on the plane and gets his baggy green. Then Joe Root is his first Test wicket, he takes a four-fer on debut, and makes 81, with nine sixes.

"All of Edgbaston and all of Pakistan were on their feet!"

'Razaullah showed the beauty of Pakistan's raw talent'

Mumtaz praised the spirit that Razaullah embodied, especially in the face of an off-field crisis that saw seven changes to the tourists' squad and a head coach axed ahead of the third Test after two heavy losses to begin the series.

"He showed the beauty of Pakistan and their raw talent - even he doesn't know what he's capable of!

"He's come off the plane and has absolutely no baggage. Yes he has a first-class hundred in dramatic fashion, but his hand speed is so quick he is ripping through the ball.

"He sits so deep in the crease and barely any of his boundaries are mishits - all of his sixes were monsters.

"That's the spark, the energy, the exuberance of youth that you are looking for.

"There was a smile on his face and he was not overwhelmed by the occasion. He didn't look in awe of it - he almost looked like he believed."

Razaullah: I just had to bat - you got to enjoy it!

Pakistan debutant Razaullah, using Urooj Mumtaz' translations after speaking to Sky Sports in Urdu:

"I just had to bat, you are the ones who get to enjoy it!

"I was planning to take it longer and deeper - 81 runs is not bad though!

"The ball was in my slot - I was eyeing that up and trying to provide support for the other batters and trying to take it as deep as possible - I broke both my bats and wore down my third.

"There was no point at which I didn't enjoy it or when I was scared.

"I was wanting the strike, and overall I wanted to keep the strike as long as possible to get Pakistan another day."

Mumtaz praised the role of fellow tail-ender Abbas - who notched his highest-ever Test score - in the partnership, and refused to rule out a miraculous comeback for Pakistan:

"To put one youngster in to bat with one stalwart of the game in Mohammed Abbas who is now on the honours board at Lord's after an eight-year gap between fifers," Mumtaz added.

"Abbas said 'I'm not just a seam bowler - I'm going to hit a few down the ground,' and he did!

"It all just amalgamates to show what could have happened if Pakistan had the temperament, the flair and the technique to back it up for the twelve-odd days of cricket we've had.

"If anyone is a betting person, after what's happened today, it's almost like that dimming light has been ignited again.

"You never know [what will happen]. Razaullah had a four-fer on debut [in England's first innings], and he provides a point of difference with pace.

"They'll have to believe - there will have to be words of wisdom - and also know that there's not too much to be said.

"They can leave it at that, watch some tapes and come back tomorrow with hope."
